correctness.rationale: Let finite projective plane order q>=2 have v=q^2+q+1 points and lines. Every covered point in a geodetic interval is selected or lies on a selected line, and dually every covered line is selected or through a selected point. For a selected a-point, b-line set, the union bounds v≤a+1+bq and v≤b+1+aq imply a+b≥2q. Equality forces a=b=q, all q selected lines concurrent at some x, and the q selected points exactly on omitted line L excluding x; conversely shortest paths cover every vertex for each such incident flag. Thus g=2q and precisely v(q+1) bases. For two flags, same x or same L yields distance q+1 (2q choices); no cross-incidence yields 2q−2 (q^3 choices); single cross-incidence yields 2q (2q^2 choices). Flag adjacency for q>=3 is connected at q+1; for q2 opposite flags at distance2 yield connectedness, with smaller threshold graph edgeless. Independently enumerate ALL vertex subsets through size4 in Fano incidence graph and size6 in ternary PG(2,3), reconstruct full shortest-path union, finding no smaller geodetic sets, exactly 21 and 52 min bases and exact distance counts. Finite q2,q3 tests do not replace proof for arbitrary plane including non-Desarguesian.
